variants.headline: A friend in the {{era}}: {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}}, a friend of ours, has left the {{former}} behind and entered the {{era}}. In its market squares the criers have been reading the same proclamation since dawn, and the crowd keeps asking them to begin again. Our traders should take note: a neighbor with new tools will soon want new goods.

variants.headline: A friendly power enters the {{era}}
body: A nation friendly to ours has passed out of the {{former}} and into the {{era}}, though no one here can yet say which nation. The rider who brought the dispatch had the date and the age right and the name wrong, or perhaps never had it. Until a second rider comes, the paper will print the age and leave the name to the next dispatch.

variants.headline: A friend crosses into the {{era}}
body: We are informed by letters from the friendly courts that {{civilization}} has lately passed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}, and that its scholars have taken up the work of the new age. The envoy who writes to us asks whether we should care to see the new charts, a courtesy we accept with pleasure. It is no small thing for a neighbor to grow in knowledge while keeping its old manners, and we count the friendship the better for it.

variants.headline: A new age in {{civilization}}, they say
body: They say the first any of us knew of it was a peddler who came down from the hills with a new sort of clasp on his coat and would not say where he got it. {{civilization}} has gone into the {{era}}, and the peddlers are always the last to tell and the first to show.

variants.headline: Of {{civilization}}'s entry into the {{era}}
body: In this season {{civilization}} departed the {{former}} and entered the {{era}}, and its nearest city is set down in our rolls at {{distance}} from our own. The keeper of the frontier road was instructed to note every crossing at the boundary stone. No breach of the peace was recorded.

variants.headline: What a friend's new era means
body: Our friend has entered the {{era}}, and the {{former}} is behind it. Our professors have already written to colleagues there about an exchange of students, though no reply has come back. A friendship that carries scholars as well as goods is worth more than a treaty that carries neither.

variants.headline: New learning on the frontier: {{tech}}
body: {{team}} has learned {{tech}}, and its cities stand close enough that its caravans are a common sight on our roads. At the frontier market, buyers have begun asking whether goods made the new way will soon be for sale. Our own craftsmen will need an answer before their customers find one.

variants.headline: New knowledge in {{team}}: {{tech}}
body: {{team}} now share {{tech}}, and the news reached us from two directions at once. Each court credits the other with the discovery, which is a polite way of saying that nobody will name the scholar. What matters here is that the knowledge now sits on both sides of a shared border.

variants.headline: A neighbor's new learning
body: In {{team}}, {{tech}} has been taken up, and the workshops there have gone quiet about it. A carter who hauls for them says the gates close earlier now and the lamps burn past midnight. We should read that as old purposes fitted with new tools, and ask what our own workshops are doing at midnight.

variants.headline: Notice to the learned: {{tech}} abroad
body: The printers give notice that {{tech}} is now practiced in {{team}}, whose lands lie near our own. Any scholar who can show the report false is invited to call at the office and set the record right. Until then the notice stands as received.

variants.headline: New learning across the fence
body: The argument started at the well and moved to the bakery by midmorning: {{tech}} has reached {{team}}, and nobody could agree on what it would do to the price of bread. The baker's answer settled it. "Whatever it is," she said, "they will want it before we do, and they will pay us to carry it."

variants.headline: The lamp next door
body: {{tech}} burns at the neighbor's hearth. Our own fire must be tended the harder.

variants.headline: Our nation enters the {{era}}
body: Our nation has entered the {{era}}. At the shipyard the foreman has pinned the old drawings to the wall and told the apprentices to copy them before they fade. Nobody has said what the new age will ask of them, but they have kept the old plans close.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{era}} is ours
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The old age is behind us and the {{era}} is here. From the capital to the last farm on the frontier, one country stands in it together. Tell your children tonight: the {{era}} is ours.

variants.headline: The {{era}} begins tonight
body: The nation is in the {{era}} tonight. In the schools, teachers are asking pupils a new question: what will you be able to do that your parents could not? Nobody has an answer yet. The country has a whole age to work it out.

variants.headline: The record of our passage into the {{era}}
body: In this year the nation passed from the former age into the {{era}}. The scribes entered the date in the great register, and the wardens lit the lamps at every shrine. Let the record show that we came into the new age with thanks, and not with boasting.

variants.headline: The bells rang all morning
body: Madam Editor, the bells have hardly stopped since we entered the {{era}}, and my neighbors speak as though the morning arranged itself. It did not. Clerks, surveyors and schoolmasters worked for years to bring us here, and none of them will stand on a balcony. Let the city thank them by name while they can still hear it.

variants.headline: The scholars finish {{tech}}
body: Our scholars have completed {{tech}}. The first clean copy went to the {{terms.civic.government}} this morning, and the second is already promised to a printer in the capital. The third copy, as usual, cannot be found.

variants.headline: Who can teach {{tech}} next?
body: {{tech}} is finished, and the useful question is who can teach it. One of the demonstrators has begun writing out the steps for a colleague in a town that missed the trials, in language plain enough for a first-year pupil. A discovery kept in one room is a curiosity; the same discovery taught in ten rooms is a national asset.

variants.headline: One more for the home team
body: We have {{tech}} now. No ceremony, no day off, no speech from anyone important. The country can do one more thing this week than it could last week.

variants.headline: Notice: {{tech}} is finished
body: Notice is given that our scholars have carried {{tech}} through to its end. The first sheets are drying at the press, and a copy has been set aside for the archive before any other is sold. The {{era}} may count this among its finished works, though the hands that did it will not be remembered by name.

variants.headline: At the market, the word is {{tech}}
body: By the time the mayor's clerk reached the market with the news, half the stalls already had it: {{tech}} is ours. A porter wanted to know what it would put in his bowl, and nobody could tell him. The crowd cheered anyway, then went back to haggling.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} crosses into the {{era}}
body: {{civilization}} has moved out of the {{former}} and into the {{era}}. A wool merchant here has asked her agent there to send a sample of whatever the new workshops are turning out before she promises anything to her customers. Caution like that is why her shop is still open.

variants.headline: A rival power enters the {{era}}
body: A rival has left the {{former}} and entered the {{era}}, and our dispatches cannot name it. The seal was unbroken and the date was plain, but the name had been rubbed from the first line. The clerks have filed the report under the age and left the name blank.

variants.headline: A rival leaves the {{former}}
body: Advices from abroad report that {{civilization}}, which is no particular friend of ours, has passed out of the {{former}} into the {{era}}. A bookseller in this city has set their new grammars on the same shelf as ours, without comment. Whether the crossing calls for congratulation or for care, we leave to readers who know that country better than we do.

variants.headline: Up the road, a new era
body: {{civilization}} has entered the {{era}}, and its nearest city is {{distance}} from ours. Nobody has moved a border stone. Nobody has marched. The country on the other side of the hill simply knows more this week than it did last, and that is how these things start.

variants.headline: It is told of {{civilization}}
body: It is told that when the {{era}} came to {{civilization}}, the old men asked for the old calendars to be kept, and the young ones laughed. The calendars were shelved, and the counting began again. What the new age cost them, the tellers leave out.

variants.headline: A rival enters the {{era}}. And us?
body: Look at {{civilization}}, {{terms.civic.people}}: it has entered the {{era}}, and its {{player.civic.government}} will soon be asked what the crossing cost. Put the same question to ours, and do not accept a speech for an answer. What are we paying, and who signed the bill? A {{terms.civic.government}} that cannot name the price has already lost the argument.

variants.headline: First in learning: {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}} now holds first place in learning, with {{count|known technology|known technologies}}. A bookseller in this city says readers have begun asking for copies of its journals before the ink on them is dry. First place is easy to lose, but the books that won it will still be read here next year.

variants.headline: A new nation stands first in learning
body: A new nation has taken first place in learning, with {{count|known technology|known technologies}}, and our dispatches have not brought its name. The reading room has already had a request to borrow its journals overnight. The librarian said yes, on condition that the borrower returns them before the name arrives.

variants.headline: The learning count, restated
body: First place held by: {{civilization}}
Arts and sciences counted: {{count}}
Rivals above it: none

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: {{civilization}} leads the world in learning with {{count|art or science|arts and sciences}}. So does someone else, apparently. The podium is going to be crowded.

variants.headline: Two ways to count learning
body: The nation at the top of the tally holds {{count|art or science|arts and sciences}}, but a tally is a thin thing to judge a school by. In one old library, the shelf for a much-studied art is worn smooth while another shelf still smells of glue. A rival further down the list may have taught more pupils in the arts we share, and its benches are the fuller for it.
